metaDescription: Six OttLite lighted magnifiers compared by lens power, spot viewer, mounting and portability, from floor and desk lamps to clip-on and pocket models.
introParagraphs: OttLite built its name on lamps designed to reduce eyestrain, and its magnifier line applies the same idea to crafts, reading and hobby work. The range is broader than many shoppers expect, with floor lamps, desk lamps, a clip on, a neck cord model and a pocket magnifier. We compared six OttLite models to show which one fits which job.

The lens powers are modest and practical. The ClearSun floor and table lamp has a 5 inch 2X lens with a 4X spot viewer, the Classic CFL task lamp has a 2X magnifier, and the Space Saving desk lamp has a 3 inch 1.75x lens with a 4x spot viewer. The Clip On is 3x with a 5x spot viewer, the 4 Inch Hands Free is 1.5x with a 4.25x spot viewer, and the Pocket model is a 3.5x folding magnifier.

We evaluated each pick based on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at lens power, spot viewers, mounting and portability. The sections below explain how to match an OttLite to sewing, reading or travel, instead of simply ranking the line.

products.name: OttLite 2-in-1 ClearSun LED Floor and Table Lamp

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Floor lamp or table lamp, flexible neck

products.description:
The ClearSun is the most complete OttLite magnifier here. It pairs a 5 inch optical grade 2X lens with a 4X spot viewer outlined with LED lights, and it works as either a floor lamp or a table lamp. The flexible neck and an integrated handle make it easy to move and position.

OttLite's ClearSun LED technology is designed to provide balanced, natural light and reduce eyestrain, which is the brand's main selling point. A 2X lens gives a wide, comfortable view for reading and crafts, while the spot viewer handles finer detail. The tradeoff is that 2X is a gentle power, so very tiny print will still need a higher spot viewer, and the unit is a full size lamp rather than a travel piece.

Setup is a short assembly, and cleaning is a soft cloth on the lens. Compared with the Space Saving lamp, you get a bigger lens and a floor option but at a larger size. Against the Clip On, you gain a bigger window but lose its portability.
products.bestFor: A main craft or reading lamp with a large lens
pros: Large 5 inch 2X optical grade lens
4X spot viewer outlined with LEDs
Works as a floor lamp or table lamp
Integrated handle for easy moving
cons: 2X is a gentle power for tiny print
Full size lamp is not a travel item

products.name: OttLite LED Clip-On Magnifier Lamp
products.description:
The Clip On is the most flexible OttLite because it has two interchangeable heads. You can use the lighted magnifier or swap in a book light, and the clip lets it attach to a table edge, a sewing machine or a headboard. The magnifier is an LED illuminated 3x optical grade lens with a 5x spot viewer.

The 3x and 5x combination is a good match for reading and sewing, because 3x keeps a wide view while 5x handles small detail. High contrast, low glare illumination is the brand's focus, which helps with comfort over time. The tradeoff is the smaller window than the floor lamps, and a clip needs a suitable edge to attach to.

Setup is as simple as clipping it on, and cleaning is a soft cloth on the lens. Compared with the ClearSun, you get higher power and portability but a smaller lens. Against the Space Saving lamp, you trade a freestanding base for a clip and a second head.
products.bestFor: Sewing machines, bedside reading and tight workspaces
pros: 3x lens with a 5x spot viewer
Swappable magnifier and book light heads
Clip on mount fits many edges
Low glare illumination
cons: Smaller window than the floor lamps
Needs a suitable edge to clip onto

products.name: OttLite Space-Saving LED Magnifier Desk Lamp
products.description:
The Space Saving lamp lives up to its name. It combines a lamp and a built in magnifier, giving you a 3 inch 1.75x optical grade lens with a 4x spot viewer. It folds down neatly for storage or travel and includes a lens cover to protect the glass.

The low power of 1.75x gives a wide, relaxed view, which suits reading and needlework where you want to see the surrounding stitches. The spot viewer adds 4x when you need it. The tradeoff is the modest lens size and power, so it will not suit very fine detail work, and a foldable lamp is less stable than a heavy base.

Setup is unfolding the arm, and the lens cover keeps dust off during storage. Compared with the ClearSun, you get a smaller lens but a much smaller footprint. Against the Clip On, you gain a freestanding base but lose the swappable book light head.
pros: Folds flat for storage or travel
3 inch optical grade lens with a 4x spot viewer
Includes a lens cover
Combined lamp and magnifier in one
cons: Lighter base is less stable than floor models

products.name: OttLite 13-Watt Classic CFL Magnifier Task Lamp
products.description:
The Classic CFL is a traditional task lamp with an integrated 2x optical grade magnifier. The shade adjusts from 11.5 to 19.5 inches in height, and a 360 degree swiveling 5 inch base lets you aim it where you need. A built in carry handle and a fold up design make it portable.

This model uses a 13 watt CFL bulb rather than an LED, which is older technology and runs warmer than LED lamps. That is the main tradeoff, along with a bulkier build. The adjustable height is a real strength, since it lets you raise the light for larger projects and lower it for close work.

Cleaning is a soft cloth on the lens and shade. Compared with the ClearSun, you get a lower power but a portable, foldable form. Against the Space Saving lamp, you gain more height adjustment but a heavier, hotter bulb.
products.bestFor: Crafters who move a lamp between tables and rooms
pros: Shade adjusts from 11.5 to 19.5 inches
360 degree swiveling base
Built in carry handle and folding design
2x optical grade magnifier
cons: CFL bulb is older tech than LED

products.name: OttLite 4-Inch Hands-Free LED Magnifier
products.description:
The 4 Inch Hands Free is the simplest way to keep a magnifier close without holding it. It hangs from an adjustable neck cord, and no slip rubberized feet let it stand on a table or rest on your chest. The 4 inch rimless acrylic lens gives 1.5x magnification with a 4.25x spot viewer for finer detail.

The rimless lens avoids a frame that would block your view, and the low power gives a wide, comfortable field. It is built for needlepoint, reading and jewelry making. The tradeoff is that the 1.5x is very gentle, so people who need stronger help will need the spot viewer for most tasks.

Cleaning is a soft cloth on the lens, and the neck cord adjusts to your height. Compared with the Clip On, you get a hands free neck design but less power. Against the Pocket model, you gain a larger lens at the cost of portability.
products.bestFor: Needlepoint and reading while moving around
pros: Adjustable neck cord keeps it hands free
4 inch rimless lens gives a wide view
No slip rubberized feet for table use
4.25x spot viewer for detail

products.name: OttLite Pocket LED Magnifier with Carabiner Clip
products.description:
The Pocket model is the lightest OttLite in this guide. It is a folding 3.5x magnifier with an LED that lights instantly when you open it, and it turns off automatically when you fold it away. A carabiner clip lets you attach it to a bag, keys or belt loop.

The auto on and off feature is a thoughtful design for people who do not want to hunt for a switch or run down a battery. A 3.5x power is enough for most menus, labels and mail. The tradeoff is the small lens, which shows only a few words at a time, and the listing does not give a lens diameter.

Cleaning is a soft cloth on the lens, and the fold keeps it protected. Compared with the Clip On, you gain pocket portability but lose hands free use. Against the 4 Inch Hands Free, you get a higher power in a much smaller package.
products.bestFor: Reading menus and labels away from home
pros: Light turns on when you open it
Automatic off when folded away
3.5x power for fine print
Carabiner clip attaches to a bag
cons: Small lens shows only a few words

buyingCriteria.criterion: Choose the right power and spot viewer
buyingCriteria.explanation: Most OttLite magnifiers pair a gentle main lens with a stronger spot viewer, such as the ClearSun's 2X with 4X or the Clip On's 3x with 5x. Higher power narrows the field of view, so use the lowest power that works. A common starting point is 3.5x for mail and 5x for fine print. The main lens handles general viewing and the spot viewer handles detail.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Decide on a lamp or a handheld style
buyingCriteria.explanation: A lamp like the ClearSun, Classic CFL or Space Saving holds a lens steady over your work, which helps with arthritis or tremor. A pocket model like the 3.5x is quick but needs a grip. Think about whether you work in one place or move around. Lamps suit regular tasks.

OttLite emphasizes balanced, natural light designed to reduce eyestrain. The ClearSun uses ClearSun LED, the Classic CFL uses a 13 watt compact fluorescent, and the others use LED. LED runs cooler and lasts longer than CFL. Choose LED unless you already own a compatible CFL lamp.

A floor lamp like the ClearSun stands on its own, the Clip On attaches to an edge, and the Space Saving folds flat. The Classic CFL has a 360 degree swiveling 5 inch base and adjusts from 11.5 to 19.5 inches. A clip needs a sturdy edge, while a foldable lamp is lighter and less stable. Match the mount to your space.

A bigger lens shows more of the work. The ClearSun offers 5 inches, the Space Saving 3 inches and the 4 Inch Hands Free 4 inches. The Pocket model is much smaller. Pick the largest lens that fits your space, because a small lens forces you to move the work often.

The Space Saving lamp folds and includes a lens cover, the Classic CFL has a handle and folds, and the Pocket model clips to a bag. If you craft away from home, portability matters more than lens size. A lens cover protects the glass from scratches during travel. Pack the lamp in a padded bag so the arm is not bent in transit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Magnification
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the main lens and spot viewer of each pick, from the Pocket 3.5x to the Clip On's 3x and 5x. We checked how clearly each listing states the power. Useful pairings scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lighting
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the lighting type, from ClearSun LED to the Classic CFL. LED models scored higher for cooler running and longer life. Balanced, low glare light was the priority.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mounting and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed floor, table, clip and neck cord designs for steadiness. The ClearSun's floor stand and the Classic CFL's swiveling base scored well. Clip and foldable models depend on the surface.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked folding, handles, covers and size. The Space Saving lamp and Pocket model stood out. Heavier lamps lost points for travel.

howWeEvaluated.title: Strongest versus most basic pick
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the ClearSun, with its 5 inch 2X lens, 4X spot viewer and floor option, against the Pocket model, a simple 3.5x folder. The ClearSun earns Best Overall for a main lamp, while the Pocket model is right for travel. Value and ease of use were weighed alongside the feature gap.

rows: Menus and labels on the go

cards.label: Lamp styles
cards.text: The ClearSun, Classic CFL, Space Saving and Clip On hold a lens and light in place. They suit regular crafts and reading. Choose these if you work in one spot.

cards.label: Neck and pocket styles
cards.text: The 4 Inch Hands Free and Pocket models travel with you but have smaller lenses or lower stability. Recommendation: pick a lamp for regular work, and a neck or pocket model for portability.

rows: Instant LED that turns off when folded

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A wide, low power lens with a spot viewer for fine stitches, and a stable mount or neck cord that keeps both hands free.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The ClearSun suits best, with a 5 inch 2X lens and a 4X spot viewer. The 4 Inch Hands Free is the alternative if you prefer a neck cord.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You craft regularly and want a large lens and stable base. The ClearSun and Classic CFL give size and height flexibility.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need occasional magnification. The Pocket model and 4 Inch Hands Free cover basics at lower cost.

faq.q: How do I choose between OttLite models?
faq.a: Start with where you will use it. A lamp like the ClearSun or Clip On suits a regular craft or reading spot, while the Pocket model travels. Then choose the power, from the gentle 1.5x to the 3.5x pocket lens, based on your task.
They span a range from the lowest-cost Pocket model to the premium ClearSun. Lamps cost more than neck or pocket styles. Check the current price on Amazon before deciding, since it changes often.

A spot viewer is a small, stronger lens inside the main lens, such as the 4X on the ClearSun or the 5x on the Clip On. It gives more power for fine detail while the main lens keeps a wide view. Use it for tiny print or stitches.

LED runs cooler and lasts longer, which is why most OttLite models use it. The Classic CFL uses a 13 watt compact fluorescent bulb, which is older technology. Choose LED unless you prefer the Classic CFL's adjustable shade.

faq.q: Can I use these for reading in bed?
faq.a: The Clip On is the best fit, with a book light head and a clip that attaches to a headboard or table. The ClearSun's floor option also works beside a chair. Keep the cord out of walking paths.

faq.q: How do I clean the lens?
faq.a: Use a soft cloth and avoid paper towels, which can scratch acrylic. Use the lens cover on the Space Saving lamp when storing it. Keep the lens away from dust and direct sun.
